act: AIFC Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Terrorist Financing and Sanctions Rules (AML)

The AFSA online rulebook (as displayed on 23 October 2026) dates its AML articles 12 December 2021 (Chapter 11-1: 4 January 2024) and differs in binding rules: 6.6.1(d) reads "terminate or suspend" instead of "terminate"; 4.3.2(e) (transactions aimed at cashing out money obtained by criminal means) is missing; 5.1.5 prints its second paragraph twice and lacks the first paragraph. The amending instrument of 15 December 2024 is not published.

act: AIFC Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Terrorist Financing and Sanctions Rules (AML)
title: AML 2.2(d) and Annex 1 define "senior management" differently
summary: AML 2.2(d) says that "In these Rules 'senior management' means" every member of executive management, including every member of the Governing Body. Annex 1, which AML 1.6 names as the place of definitions, defines it as "a high-level executive who oversees the operations and performance of one or more departments". Responsibility under 2.2(a) and approvals for politically exposed persons depend on which definition applies.

title: AML Guidance after 13.1.3 cites GEN 2.1.2 for the MLRO appointment; it is now GEN 2.1.1(1)(d)
summary: The Guidance says "Under GEN 2.1.2., the MLRO function is a mandatory appointment." In the current General Rules GEN 2.1.2(1) is omitted and the MLRO appointment is GEN 2.1.1(1)(d).

act: AIFC Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Terrorist Financing and Sanctions Rules (AML)
title: AML Guidance refers to Chapter 6 for risk assessments; they are in Chapters 4 and 5
summary: Guidance (k) after AML 4.3.3 and Guidance (j) after AML 6.3.4 refer to the customer risk assessment "under Chapter 6", and the sanctions Guidance (g) to "the risk assessments under Chapters 5 and 6". AML 1.5(d) places the customer risk assessment in Chapter 5; Chapter 6 contains none.

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
title: FEES Schedule 8, 8.6: the consolidated text omits words adopted by Amendments No. 17
summary: Amendments No. 17 (13 November 2025) inserted 8.6 as "50% of an application fee for change of control payable under Schedule 1 of FEES". The consolidated V18 and the AFSA online rulebook omit "for change of control". The heading of 8.6 still ties the fee to change of control, so the meaning survives, but the published body text differs from the adopted one.

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
location: FEES Schedule 6, table 6.1, row 'Operating a Digital Asset Trading Facility'
title: FEES Schedule 6, table 6.1 (Digital Asset Trading Facility): no rule for an average daily trading value of exactly 500 000 USD
summary: The variable fee is "not applicable" where the average daily trading value is "less than 500 000 USD" and is the greater of the trading levy and 5 000 USD where it is "more than 500 000 USD". A value of exactly 500 000 USD is covered by no branch, while the outcomes on either side differ (0 USD and at least 5 000 USD for the quarter).

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
location: FEES Schedule 6, table 6.2, crowdfunding platform rows
title: FEES Schedule 6, table 6.2 (crowdfunding platforms): no rule for funds raised of exactly 1 million USD
summary: The variable fee is "not applicable" where "the funds raised is less than 1 million USD", and a levy applies to the whole amount where "the funds raised is more than 1 million USD". Funds raised of exactly 1 million USD in a quarter are covered by no branch, while the outcomes on either side differ. The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0004 raises the threshold to 5.3, 5.5 and 5.8 million USD for 2027, 2028 and 2029 with the same wording ("less than" and "more than"), so the gap moves to those amounts.

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
title: FEES 1.3 refers to Schedule 6 for Approved Individual application fees; Schedule 6 has none
summary: FEES 1.3 says Approved Individual fees are "as specified in Schedules 1, 2 or 6". Schedule 6 sets annual supervision fees only. Approved Individual fees are in Schedules 1 and 2, in Schedule 3 (change of MLRO, Audit Principal) and in Schedule 8 (FinTech Lab, 200 USD). Amendments No. 12 replaced "3 or 4" with "or 6" in 2022.

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
title: FEES Schedule 6, 6.4: the Recognised Non-AIFC Member trading value fee is ambiguous for members on several platforms
summary: The trading value fee applies to members "whose trading value is over 25 million USD per quarter on each trading platform". For a member above the threshold on one platform and below it on another, the text can mean that no fee is due (not over the threshold on each platform) or that a fee is due per platform; the base ("0.001% of trading value") does not say whether it is per platform or in total.

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
location: FEES Schedule 1, rule 1.1-1 (Amendments No. 14.1 of 9 December 2023)
title: FEES Schedule 1, 1.1-1: the exception for Operating a Digital Asset Trading Facility is printed but was never enacted
summary: Amendments No. 14.1 (9 December 2023) inserted 1.1-1 (additional application fee for Digital Assets activities) without an exception; the same instrument put an exception for Operating a Digital Asset Trading Facility only into 6.1-1. Consolidated versions V15 to V18 print the exception in 1.1-1 as well, and we could not find it in any of the published amending instruments Nos. 12 to 17. Whether a Digital Asset Trading Facility applicant owes the additional fee (now 2 800 USD) depends on which text is right; a consolidated version cannot change legal effect (section 19(2) of the AIFC Regulations on AIFC Acts). The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0004 amends 1.1-1 again (the fixed amount is replaced by a table) and prints the words "except for the Regulated Activity of Operating a Digital Asset Trading Facility" as existing text, not as an insertion.

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
title: FEES 3.1.2 and 3.1.4(b): the initial supervision fee runs from "the grant of the Licence", which recognised Non-AIFC bodies never receive
summary: Before Amendments No. 17 the due date ran from "the commencement of operations", which fitted every payer. Since then the initial annual supervision fee is due "within 21 days of the date of the grant of the Licence" and is pro-rated from that date. FEES 3.1.1 also makes Recognised Non-AIFC Market Institutions and Members pay the fee, but they are recognised by an order under the Framework Regulations, not licensed under Part 3, so the specific due date and the pro-rating do not fit them.

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
title: FEES Schedule 1, table 1.2: footnote marker "Fee (USD)*" without a footnote
summary: Amendments No. 17 deleted both the asterisk and the footnote of the modification fee tables in Schedules 1, 2 and 3. V18 and the online rulebook removed the footnote everywhere and the asterisk in Schedules 2 and 3, but kept "Fee (USD)*" in Schedule 1, table 1.2.

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
title: FEES 4.1.2 still says the fee for extracts will be set "at a later date"
summary: Amendments No. 6 (27 December 2019) made the fee in FEES 4.1.1 one "specified in Schedule 5-1" (the "Processing inquiries" row), but left FEES 4.1.2: "The Registrar of Companies may determine the amount of the fee specified in FEES 4.1.1 at a later date."

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
title: FEES Schedules 10 and 11: no start date and no cap for the daily surcharge on unpaid late fees
summary: "Non-payment of the late fee within 30 calendar days incurs a further late payment fee equal to 10% of the late fee for each calendar day" (5% in Schedule 11). The text does not say from which day the 30 days run (the contravention, the end of the 3 or 5 business days, or an invoice) and sets no cap on the surcharge (the AFSA may waive fees under FEES 5.1.3).

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
title: FEES 1.2.5(a), 1.2.6(a) and Schedule 7 refer to each other; no amount is set
summary: FEES 1.2.5(a) and 1.2.6(a) charge "the application fees specified in Schedule 7", and Schedule 7 says that the Chief Executive Officer "may determine the amount of fee specified in 1.2.5 (a) and 1.2.6.(a)". No amount appears in the Rules themselves, while section 9(7) of the Framework Regulations speaks of a fee "prescribed in the Rules".

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
location: Schedule 6, table 6.1, row 'Providing Money Services**', variable fee bullet 1
title: FEES Schedule 6, table 6.1 (Providing Money Services, from 2027): measurement period of the "annual transaction value" is not set
summary: From 1 January 2027 the variable fee is "calculated on a quarterly basis", but both the threshold (280 million USD) and the base are "the annual transaction value" at "0.0015% p.a.". The text does not say which year's value is used at each quarter or how quarterly charges and any year-end adjustment are worked out. The deferral to 2027 is in a footnote, which is not part of an AIFC Act (section 26 of the AIFC Regulations on AIFC Acts).

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
title: Fees Rules V15: cover date "as of 9 December 2022" is that of V14; two instruments numbered 14.1
summary: The cover of V15 and its label on aifc.kz read "with amendments as of 9 December 2022", the date already used for V14. The instruments consolidated in V15 are dated 10 September 2023, 10 September 2023 and 9 December 2023, and two of them are both numbered "Amendments No. 14.1".

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
location: aifc.kz Fees Rules page, list of versions (V13) — the Amendments list has A11 then A13
title: aifc.kz: the Fees Rules page does not link Amendments No. 12 (1 May 2022)
summary: The list of amending instruments on the Fees Rules page goes from A11 to A13. Amendments No. 12 (approved 24 April 2022, in force 1 May 2022), which introduced the annual supervision fees, late fees and FinTech Lab fees, is in the site's media library but is not linked from the page.

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
location: Schedule 6, table 6.1, row 'Dealing in Investments as Agent**'
title: FEES Schedule 6, table 6.1 (Dealing in Investments as Agent): "assets under brokerage" is not defined
summary: The quarterly levy of 0.0005% applies to "the amount of the assets under brokerage" above 490 million USD. The term is not defined in FEES or in the Glossary, and it is not used in any other AFSA rulebook, so it is unclear whether it means client assets held in brokerage accounts or the volume executed.

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
title: Variable fees: the payment deadline can expire before the invoice is issued
summary: Variable fees are "paid within 21 days after the issuance of an invoice by the AFSA, but no later than within 1 month following each corresponding quarter". If the invoice is issued late in the following month, or after it, the payer may have fewer than 21 days or the deadline may precede the invoice, and the 1% per month increase under FEES 5.1.2 can start before the invoice arrives.

act: AIFC Fees Rules (FEES), AIFC Rules No. FR0007 of 2017, V18
location: AIFC Regulations on AIFC Acts s.26(1)(a)
title: FEES: several fees and payment terms are set in "Notes" and footnotes, which are not part of an AIFC Act
summary: Section 26(1)(a) of the AIFC Regulations on AIFC Acts says that "a footnote, endnote or other note" is not part of an AIFC Act, even if inserted by an amending act (section 26(2)). In FEES the application fee for change of control (1 400 USD), the Approved Individual fee (500 USD), the quarterly payment of variable fees and the deferral of some fees to 1 January 2027 appear under "Notes" headings or in footnotes.

act: AIFC General Rules (GEN), V20
title: GEN Schedule 1, paragraph 4(2): two activity names that do not exist
summary: Paragraph 4(2) incorporates into Managing a Collective Investment Scheme activities constituting "Dealing as Agent" and "Dealing as Principal". Schedule 1 defines "Dealing in Investments as Agent" (paragraph 2) and "Dealing in Investments as Principal" (paragraph 1); the Glossary does not define the two shorter names. The wording has been there since the initial 2017 release. The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0001 (Annex 2) corrects a third name in the same paragraph ("Managing Assets" to "Managing Investments") but keeps these two.

act: AIFC General Rules (GEN), V20
title: GEN 2.2.9: the duty on an Approved Individual leaving binds only "the Authorised Firm"
summary: GEN 2.2.9 is triggered when an Approved Individual ceases to be employed "by an Authorised Person", but the duty to request withdrawal of the status within seven days and to report the reasons falls on "the Authorised Firm". An Authorised Person also includes an Authorised Market Institution, to which GEN 2 applies, so no one is bound when an Authorised Market Institution's Approved Individual leaves. Paragraph (b) of the same rule already says "the Authorised Person".

act: AIFC General Rules (GEN), V20
title: AFSA online rulebook, GEN 4.3.2: the integrity principle is printed under the heading of Principle 2
summary: In GEN V20 (aifc.kz) 4.3.2 requires each Approved Individual and Designated Individual to "act with due skill, care and diligence". On the AFSA online rulebook the text under "4.3.2. Principle 2 - Due skill, care and diligence" is the integrity sentence of 4.3.1, so the due skill principle for individuals is missing online.

act: AIFC General Rules (GEN), V20
location: GEN 1.1.2, Guidance: AFSA discretion to waive requirements / page 4
title: GEN Guidance after 1.1.2 cites section 32(4) of the Framework Regulations; section 32 has no subsections
summary: The Guidance refers to a waiver "pursuant to section 32(4) of the Framework Regulations". Section 32 (Financial technology) is a single paragraph; the power to waive requirements as to form and content is section 31(4).

act: AIFC General Rules (GEN), V20
title: GEN 1.3.3-1 cites section 41(1) of the Framework Regulations, which sets only a fit-and-proper criterion
summary: GEN 1.3.3-1 assesses whether an Ancillary Service Provider can be effectively supervised "for the purposes of section 41(1) of the Framework Regulations". Section 41(1) contains only the fit-and-proper criterion, while for Authorised Firms the effective supervision criterion is a separate item (section 34(1)(c)).

act: AIFC General Rules (GEN), V20
title: GEN 6.1.4 refers to "the contract required under GEN 6.1.2"; the contract is required by GEN 6.1.3
summary: GEN 6.1.4 (lead-in, (b) and (e)) sets the terms of "the contract required under GEN 6.1.2". GEN 6.1.2 names and nominates the Skilled Person; the written contract is required by GEN 6.1.3.

act: AIFC General Rules (GEN), V20
title: GEN 2.2.7 refers to requirements made under section 43(1) of the Framework Regulations; the matching waiver power is section 42(2)
summary: GEN 2.2.7 lets a firm apply to waive "requirements made pursuant to Section 43(1)" in the light of a foreign registration or approval. Section 43(1) is the fit-and-proper criterion; the provision with the same wording about foreign approval is section 42(2), which allows waiving the requirements as to form and content under section 42(1).

act: AIFC General Rules (GEN), V20
title: GEN 6.2.4(7)(b) borrows procedures and powers from Rule 6.2.4(6), which lists only factors
summary: For a branch Bank without a home notification requirement, the first sentence of GEN 6.2.4(7)(b) applies the requirements of (4); the next words say the AFSA "must follow the same procedures, and shall have the same powers, as set out in Rule 6.2.4 (6)". Rule 6.2.4(6) is a list of factors; the procedure is in (4) and the power to object in (5).

act: AIFC General Rules (GEN), V20
location: Schedule 4 para 5(5)(c) / page 59 (identical words also in para 4(5)(c), page 58)
title: GEN Schedule 4, paragraph 5(5)(c): the investment crowdfunding delegation rule requires notice to "Borrowers or lenders"
summary: Paragraph 5(5)(c) (Operating an Investment Crowdfunding Platform) repeats paragraph 4(5)(c) of the loan crowdfunding definition: the delegate must "notify Borrowers or lenders". Paragraph 5 otherwise speaks of Issuers and Investors; for shares and other non-debt investments there is no Borrower or lender to notify.

act: AIFC General Rules (GEN), V20
title: GEN 2.2.1 and 2.3.1: the ranges of Controlled and Designated Functions are out of date
summary: GEN 2.2.1 says "The functions specified in GEN 2.2.2 to 2.2.5 are Controlled Functions", but the MLRO function is now GEN 2.2.5-1. GEN 2.3.1 says "The functions specified in GEN 2.3.2 to 2.3.4 are Designated Functions", but 2.3.4 is omitted and the Risk Manager and Internal Audit Manager functions are 2.3.5 and 2.3.6.

act: AIFC Glossary (GLO), V23
location: Glossary V23, entry "Money Laundering Reporting Officer"
title: Glossary, "Money Laundering Reporting Officer": points to GEN 2.3.4, which is omitted
summary: The Glossary defines the MLRO as "the individual performing the Designated Function identified at GEN 2.3.4". GEN 2.3.4 now reads "[intentionally omitted]"; the MLRO is a Controlled Function under GEN 2.2.5-1 and must be held by an Approved Individual (GEN 2.1.1(1)(d)).

act: AIFC Glossary (GLO), V23
title: Glossary, "Takaful Business": points to paragraph 24 of GEN Schedule 1 (Insurance Management)
summary: The Glossary defines Takaful Business as "A Regulated Activity defined in paragraph 24 of Schedule 1 of the GEN". Paragraph 24 is Insurance Management; Takaful Business is paragraph 25.

act: AIFC Glossary (GLO), V23
location: Glossary V23, entry "Operating a Loan Crowdfunding Platform"
title: Glossary, "Operating a Loan Crowdfunding Platform": points to Schedule 3 of the Framework Regulations, which no longer exists
summary: The entry reads "The Market Activity as defined in paragraph 4 of Schedule 3 of the Framework Regulations". Market Activities moved to Schedule 4 of the General Rules (Framework Regulations section 18(1)); the neighbouring entries were updated, this one was not.

act: AIFC Glossary (GLO), V23
title: Glossary, "Money Services": excludes activities "specified in paragraph 21 (3)" of GEN Schedule 1, which does not exist
summary: The definition, adopted with Amendments No. 21 (in force 13 October 2025), excludes "any of the activities specified in paragraph 21 (3) Schedule 1 of GEN". Paragraph 21 has no sub-paragraph (3); the same package of amendments moved the exclusions to paragraph 21-1.

act: AIFC Glossary (GLO), V23
location: Glossary V23, entry "Client Money Distribution Rules"
title: Glossary: three insurance client money terms point to COB 11.8, which no longer exists
summary: "Client Money Distribution Rules" ("COB 11.8.14"), "Client Money" ("COB 11.8.4") and "Segregated Client" ("COB 11.8") point to COB 11.8. Chapter 11 of the current COB ends at 11.7; the client money rules for insurance intermediation are in COB 8.5 (including 8.5.5, money held as agent of an insurer, and 8.5.15, distribution rules). The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0005 changes the fourth such entry, "Insurance Intermediary Audit Report", to refer to GEN 6.3.9, which we support, but leaves these three as they are.

act: AIFC Glossary (GLO), V23
title: Glossary, "Approved Individual": the two limbs are joined by "and"
summary: An Approved Individual is defined as an individual "(1) approved by the AFSA to carry out a Controlled Function; and (2) approved by the AFSA to be appointed by a DNFBP and Registered Auditor to carry out the MLRO function". Read literally, an individual approved only for a Controlled Function is not an Approved Individual. Section 21 of the Framework Regulations defines the term by limb (1) alone. The AFSA online Glossary shows both versions: the list has the two limbs, the term page only limb (1).

act: AIFC Glossary (GLO), V23
title: Glossary, "Authorised Investment Exchange": refers to "Operating an Investment Exchange"
summary: The definition refers to the "Market Activity of Operating an Investment Exchange". The Market Activity in GEN Schedule 4, paragraph 1, and in the Glossary itself is "Operating an Exchange". The entry "Operating a facility for Investment Tokens" uses the same name.

act: AIFC Prudential Rules for Investment Firms (PRU INV), V7
location: PRU (INV) 3.3(3), Table 3.3, row for Exempt Funds
title: PRU (Investment Firms) Table 3.3: a manager of a Single Family Office Fund without a custodian falls in two rows (USD 50,000 and USD 500,000)
summary: Amendments No. 4 (in force 1 July 2024) added "or (b) because the Fund is a Single Family Office Fund" to the USD 50,000 row of Table 3.3. The USD 500,000 row for a Collective Investment Scheme "which does not have an appointed Eligible Custodian" was not changed; its only exception is the nature of the Fund and its assets. A manager of a Single Family Office Fund without an Eligible Custodian therefore meets both rows, and the text does not say which applies. Reading both rows cumulatively gives USD 500,000 and leaves the limb added by Amendments No. 4 without effect.

act: AIFC Prudential Rules for Investment Firms (PRU INV), V7
title: PRU (Investment Firms) 1.3(10) and 6.1(2): which Chapter 6 rules apply to Externally Regulated firms
summary: Rule 1.3(10) says that "in Chapter 6, only Rule 6.6 applies" to Externally Regulated PRU Investment Firms. Rule 6.1(2) says "Other than Rules 6.5 and 6.6, this Chapter does not apply" to them, and Rule 6.5(2) contains a limitation written for them. Rule 6.5 carries the duty to notify a breach within one Business Day and the restriction on payments to Affiliates, so whether these firms are bound by it depends on which rule is read.

act: AIFC Prudential Rules for Investment Firms (PRU INV), V7
title: PRU (Investment Firms) 3.2: the definition of Capital Resources refers three times to "the Insurance Intermediary"
summary: Rule 3.2(1)(a) counts the share capital "of the PRU Investment Firm", but 3.2(1)(c) counts retained earnings and reserves "of the Insurance Intermediary", and the deductions in 3.2(2)(b)(iv) and (v) refer to the pension fund assets and own shares of "the Insurance Intermediary". The intended meaning is clear from context, but the text names a different kind of firm. The Prudential Rules for Insurance Intermediaries now say "the Authorised Firm" in the same items.

act: Constitutional Statute of the Republic of Kazakhstan on the Astana International Financial Centre and AIFC acts
location: AIFC website, page of the Constitutional Statute, download list
title: aifc.kz: the link "Constitutional Statute of the Republic of Kazakhstan kz" opens the Constitution of Kazakhstan
summary: On the Constitutional Statute page of aifc.kz the link labelled "Constitutional Statute of the Republic of Kazakhstan kz" serves constitution-of-the-rk-kz.pdf, a 48-page Kazakh text of the Constitution of the Republic of Kazakhstan.

act: Constitutional Statute of the Republic of Kazakhstan on the Astana International Financial Centre and AIFC acts
title: The Structure of the Bodies of the AIFC, §9(14): the Governor recommends judges "to the Council"
summary: Under Article 13(3-1) of the Constitutional Statute the Chairman and judges of the AIFC Court are appointed by the President on the Governor's recommendation; the AIFC Court Regulations say the same. §9(14) of the Structure of the Bodies (as of 1 July 2021) says that the Governor recommends to the Council the persons to be appointed as judges, wording that predates the 2017 amendment of the Statute.

act: Constitutional Statute of the Republic of Kazakhstan on the Astana International Financial Centre and AIFC acts
title: AFSA online rulebook: the page "Financial Services Exempt from Corporate Tax" carries no act title, number, date or adopting body
summary: The page is listed under Rules (version 1 January 2020) and states that a participant "shall not be liable for corporation tax … on income or capital" for the services in its Schedule 1. It carries no act title, number, date or adopting body, no end date (the Statute sets 1 January 2066) and no exclusion of the digital asset exchange (Article 6(3), since 2023).

act: Constitutional Statute of the Republic of Kazakhstan on the Astana International Financial Centre and AIFC acts
title: aifc.kz, The Structure of the Bodies of the AIFC: two links serve the wrong file
summary: The links "… ru (initial)" and "… with amendments as of 9 October 2017. ENG" serve the same file as the 2021 Russian consolidation ("с изменениями и дополнениями по состоянию на 1 июля 2021 года"). The initial Russian text and the 2017 English version are not available.

act: AIFC Conduct of Business Rules (COB), V17
title: AFSA online COB does not include the Amendments No. 14 changes in force since 13 January 2026
summary: Amendments No. 14 to COB commence on 13 January 2026, except the changes to COB 1.2.2, which commenced on 13 October 2025. The consolidated version V17 on aifc.kz contains them: COB 8.1.2 and 8.1.4 now cover firms that Provide Money Services, the Guidance under COB 8.2.5 refers to PMS 9, COB 15.1 has two new paragraphs, and the new COB 15.5 sets a deadline of 15 business days for Money Service complaints. The aifc.kz page for COB says that the current version can be found on the regulator's website. The AFSA online COB (checked on 23 October 2026) shows none of these changes: COB 8.1.2(a) still refers only to Investment Business, COB 15.1 has one paragraph, and there is no COB 15.5. The page shows no deleted (struck-through) text at these places.

act: AIFC Conduct of Business Rules (COB), V17
title: COB 19.5.1(c): the Insurer's claims item has no operative words
summary: COB 19.5.1(c) reads only "(including by terminating or avoiding a policy); and": there is no verb and no object. The parallel lists for Insurance Intermediaries (COB 11.7.6(c)) and Insurance Managers (COB 20.4.1(c)) read "not unreasonably reject a claim (including by terminating or avoiding a policy); and". Both the amending instrument and the consolidated text show the item with nothing before the parenthesis; it is already incomplete in Amendments No. 2 (2 December 2018), which inserted COB 19. The general claims-handling duty in 19.5.1(a) still applies.

act: AIFC Conduct of Business Rules (COB), V17
title: COB 15.5.4 points to 'paragraph 2 of COB 15.4.2', a one-paragraph rule on the content of complaint records
summary: COB 15.5.4 requires information about other means of resolving complaints, "as outlined in paragraph 2 of COB 15.4.2", to be made available on the website, at branches and in the client terms of a Money Service Provider. COB 15.4.2 ("Content of records") has a single paragraph on what a complaints record must contain; it has no paragraph 2. The duty to inform a complainant of other means of resolving the Complaint is the second paragraph of COB 15.2.5. The wrong number is already in Amendments No. 14, which inserted COB 15.5.4. The descriptive words keep the meaning.

act: AIFC Conduct of Business Rules (COB), V17
title: COB 13.2.10 heading in the consolidated texts and online reads "Principle 8 ‐ Client Money and Client Assets"; Amendments No. 11 inserted "Principle 10 – Complaints"
summary: Amendments No. 11 (in force 1 January 2024) inserted COB 13.2.9 "Principle 9 ‐ Conflicts of interest" and 13.2.10 "Principle 10 – Complaints"; the amending instrument shows both headings as new text. The consolidated versions V12 to V17 on aifc.kz and the AFSA online COB show 13.2.10 under the heading "Principle 8 ‐ Client Money and Client Assets", which is the heading of 13.2.8. The rulebook therefore has two "Principle 8" headings and no Principle 10. The text of 13.2.10 itself (complaints) is correct.
reported_to: Astana Financial Services Authority (AFSA); AIFC Authority

act: AIFC Conduct of Business Rules (COB), V17
title: COB 1.2.4 lists 'COB 15 (Record Keeping)' for Trust Service Providers: COB 15 is complaints, record keeping is COB 16
summary: COB 1.2.4 disapplies COB to Trust Service Providers except, among others, "COB 15 (Record Keeping)". Chapter 15 is "Complaints Handling and Dispute Resolution"; Chapter 16 is "Record Keeping and Internal Audit"; and section 15.4 inside Chapter 15 is "Record keeping" for complaints. The number and the label point to different provisions. The mismatch exists from the first version of COB (2017) and was kept through every later change to 1.2.4. Other exclusion rules name the chapters correctly, for example 1.2.2(g): "COB 15 (Complaints Handling and Dispute Resolution), COB 16 (Record Keeping and Internal Audit)".

act: AIFC Conduct of Business Rules (COB), V17
title: COB 2.3.1(b) lists only COB 2.5.1 and 2.5.5 and omits Undertakings assessed under COB 2.5.6
summary: COB 2.3.1(b) allows a Person to be classified as a Professional Client if it meets the requirements to be an Assessed Professional Client "in accordance with COB 2.5.1 or 2.5.5". COB 2.5.1 covers individuals and 2.5.5 joint account holders. COB 2.5.6 (Undertakings with own funds of at least USD 1 million) is not listed, although 2.5.6 itself applies "For the purposes of COB 2.3.1" and the Glossary defines Assessed Professional Client by "COB 2.5.1 and 2.5.6". The words of 2.5.6 and the Glossary keep the intended meaning, but the list in 2.3.1(b) does not match them.

act: AIFC Conduct of Business Rules (COB), V17
title: COB 8.5 was extended to Insurance Managers but the distribution waterfall and agency rule still name only the Insurance Intermediary
summary: Amendments No. 2 rewrote the old COB 11.8 as COB 8.5 for "an Insurance Intermediary or Insurance Manager", and that phrase runs through COB 8.5. Three places still name only the Insurance Intermediary: 8.5.15(2)(c) "where insufficient funds are held by the Insurance Intermediary"; 8.5.15(2)(d)(i) "trustee in bankruptcy over the Insurance Intermediary, payment must be made accordance with the AIFC Insolvency Regulations"; and 8.5.5(b) "once the money is received by the Insurance Intermediary". The Investment Business rule 8.2.16(2)(d)(i) covers "the Authorised Firm or the Nominee Company".

act: AIFC Conduct of Business Rules (COB), V17
title: Amendments No. 14 apply COB 8.2 to Money Service Providers but 'Client Money' (8.2.1, Glossary) still covers only Investment Business money
summary: Since Amendments No. 14 (13 January 2026), COB 8.1.2 and 8.1.4 require an Authorised Firm that Provides Money Services to comply with COB 8.2, and PMS 9.1 sends a Money Service Provider to a Client Money Account "as prescribed under COB 8". The intended scheme follows from these rules. But COB 8.2.1, the heading of COB 8.2 ("Client Money: Investment Business") and the Glossary definition of "Client Money" still describe only Money held in connection with Investment Business, so the definition and the heading do not match the rule that applies them.

act: AIFC Conduct of Business Rules (COB), V17
title: COB 6.1.1(a) keeps COB 6.2.9 for Market Counterparty transactions, but COB 6.2.1(a) disapplies all of COB 6.2 for them
summary: COB 6.1.1(a): COB 6 does not apply to a transaction 'it undertakes with a Market Counterparty, except for COB 6.2.9'. The table in 1.2.7 repeats the exception. COB 6.2.1(a): 'The Rules in COB 6.2 do not apply ... to any transaction which: (a) it undertakes with a Market Counterparty' - with no exception, and 6.2.9 is inside 6.2.

act: AIFC Conduct of Business Rules (COB), V17
title: COB 5.6.11 names Insurance Intermediaries for the Takaful disclosure, but COB 1.2.3 does not list it among the rules that apply to them
summary: COB 1.2.3 says that COB does not apply to Insurance Intermediaries "with the exception of COB 3, COB 4, COB 8.5 and COB 11". COB 5.6.11(1), inserted with the Takaful amendments in 2018, names "an Insurance Intermediary" among the persons who must explain the differences between Takaful and conventional contracts. When COB 8.5 was added to the list in 1.2.3, 5.6.11 was not. Because 5.6.11 names Insurance Intermediaries expressly, it is best read as applying to them, but 1.2.3 does not say so.

act: AIFC Conduct of Business Rules (COB), V17
title: Client asset rules give regulatory roles to 'the AIFC' (the Centre) where the regulator, the AFSA, is meant
summary: The Glossary defines AIFC as the Astana International Financial Centre (a territory/regime). COB nevertheless says: firms must demonstrate grounds 'to the AIFC's satisfaction' (8.2.11, 8.3.8); Client Money may be paid out in circumstances 'otherwise authorised by the AIFC' (8.2.13(e)); disclosure of 'other Distribution Event stipulated by the AIFC' (8.2.18(a)(ii)). The parallel collateral disclosure (8.3.2(d)) says 'stipulated by the AFSA', and the Glossary Distribution Event (c) is a direction by the AFSA.

act: AIFC Conduct of Business Rules (COB), V17
title: COB 8.5.13(2) and the 16.2 table use the undefined 'Insurance Bank Account'
summary: COB 8.5 requires Client Money to be held in "Client Money Accounts" (8.5.6, 8.5.9). COB 8.5.13(2) requires records of "all sums withdrawn from the Insurance Bank Account as a result of credit taken under COB 8.5.12", and the table in COB 16.2 repeats it. "Insurance Bank Account" is not defined in COB or in the Glossary and is used nowhere else. The term has been in COB since the first version (then COB 11.8.12). The meaning (the Client Money Account) can be recovered from 8.5.9 and 8.5.12.

act: AIFC Market Rules (MAR), V13
title: MAR 1.1.2(1)(b): is an offer that meets both (2)(c) and (2)(d) meant to lose the placement exemption?
summary: MAR 1.1.2(1)(b) exempts an offer by way of placement only if it satisfies "one and one only" of the conditions in (2); (1)(c) allows combinations only where one of them is (a), (b) or (m). An offer of Securities denominated in units of at least USD 100,000 (condition (d)) and issued at or above that amount also meets condition (c), because every investor pays at least USD 100,000. Read literally, such an offer is not exempt unless it also meets (a), (b) or (m), while the same offer issued below USD 100,000 per unit would be. For Exempt Securities, MAR 1.2.2(1) uses "one or more of the conditions". The words "one and one only" may be meant to stop the stacking of exemptions, but the text does not say which combinations are excluded.

act: AIFC Market Rules (MAR), V13
title: MAR 5.2.2(a) in the consolidated PDFs V9–V13 on aifc.kz still refers to itself; Amendments No. 8 changed it to MAR 5.2.1
summary: Amendments No. 8 to the Market Rules (approved 25 June 2023, in force 1 August 2023) replaced "5.2.2" with "5.2.1" in MAR 5.2.2(a) and added the closing bracket. The consolidated versions V9 (1 August 2023) to V13 (1 January 2026) published on aifc.kz applied the other edits in the same line ("of", "Investments") but still read "has the meaning given in MAR 5.2.2 (Definition of Inside Information (general); and", so the definition refers to itself. The AFSA online rulebook already reads "MAR 5.2.1". The bracketed title points to 5.2.1, so the meaning survives.
reported_to: Astana Financial Services Authority (AFSA); AIFC Authority

act: AIFC Market Rules (MAR), V13
title: MAR 5.5.2, 6.1.7, 6.2.2 and 6.4.3: references printed as "MAR 5.2.65", "MAR 6.2.21" and "MAR 5.2.6.6" name no existing rule
summary: Four references in the market abuse and disclosure chapters name rules that do not exist: "MAR 5.2.65" (5.5.2 and 6.1.7), "MAR 6.2.21" (6.2.2) and "MAR 5.2.6.6" (6.4.3). Up to V4 (14 February 2019) these places read "MAR 5.2.6" and "MAR 6.2.2"; the merged numbers first appear in V5 (2019), and we found no amending instrument that made that change. Amendments No. 6 (2020) shows "5.2.5" as new text in 6.1.7, next to a broken field code ("Error! Reference source not found."), and its text of 6.2.2 and 6.4.3 is also damaged; V7 to V13 still print "MAR 5.2.65". The AFSA online text is the same. The bracketed titles show the intended targets for three of the places: 5.2.5 (Unlawful disclosure of Inside Information) in 5.5.2 and 6.1.7, and 6.2.1 (Obligation to draw up insider lists) in 6.2.2. In 6.4.3 there is no title.
reported_to: Astana Financial Services Authority (AFSA); AIFC Authority

act: AIFC Market Rules (MAR), V13
title: MAR 6.2.2 heading refers to 'MAR 8.2.2 (Obligation to draw up insider lists)'; MAR has no chapter 8
summary: The heading of MAR 6.2.2 reads 'Reporting Entity is responsible for complying with MAR 8.2.2 (Obligation to draw up insider lists)'. MAR ends with chapter 7 and Schedules 1-4; the obligation to draw up insider lists is MAR 6.2.1. The number has been wrong since the initial version (2017) and is repeated in the table of contents and on the regulator's site.

act: AIFC Market Rules (MAR), V13
title: MAR 1.9.4(4)(a): the Expert limb of the correction defence refers to "(2)(c)", which is not about Expert statements; the Expert paragraph is (3)
summary: MAR 1.9.4(4)(a) gives a defence where, before acquisition, "a correction or, where the statement was such as is mentioned in (2)(c), the fact that the Expert was not competent or had not consented" was published. Paragraph (2)(c) is the general correction defence and describes no statement; statements made on the authority of an Expert are dealt with in (3). Read literally, the second limb of (4)(a) has no case to apply to. The same reference is already in Amendments No. 7 (29 June 2022), which inserted 1.9.3 and 1.9.4: the instrument lettered the top-level paragraphs (a) to (f) but its own cross-references already used the numbers (2) to (6), so "(2)(c)" pointed to the correction defence from the start. The DFSA and ADGM market rules from which this text comes have the same reference (DFSA MKT 2.11.1(4)(a), ADGM MKT 4.11.1(4)(a)). MAR 1.9.3 and 1.9.4 appear in the consolidated MAR (V13) on aifc.kz but not in the AFSA online rulebook (see AIFC2-MKT-13).

act: AIFC Market Rules (MAR), V13
title: MAR 5.5.3: the closing words "prior to conducting a Market Sounding" also cover the record of disclosures in (c), which can only be completed after the sounding
summary: MAR 5.5.3 lists four steps (a) to (d) and then, on a separate line after (d), the words "prior to conducting a Market Sounding". Laid out this way, the words govern the whole list. Steps (a) and (b) already carry their own timing. Step (c) requires a record of the disclosures, including "the date and time of each disclosure", which cannot be complete before the sounding. The AFSA online text joins the closing words to (d) instead. The second sentence of (c) also asks for the record to be given to "the competent authority", while (d) names the AFSA.

act: AIFC Market Rules (MAR), V13
title: MAR 2.4.5(b) refers to "a Takeover Offer under the Takeover Rules": which Takeover Rules apply?
summary: MAR 2.4.5(b) lifts the closed-period dealing ban for "undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a Takeover Offer under the Takeover Rules". The Glossary defines "Takeover Rules" as Rules prescribed by the AFSA under section 88(1)(a) of the Framework Regulations, which says that the AFSA "may prescribe" such Rules. We did not find any Takeover Rules among the acts published on aifc.kz or in the AFSA online rulebook. Chapter 11 of Part 7 of the AIFC Companies Regulations ("Protection of Minorities in Takeovers") is part of the Regulations, not Rules made by the AFSA under section 88(1)(a). If no Takeover Rules have been made, exemption (b) has nothing to apply to, and a Restricted Person would need clearance under MAR 2.4.4.

act: AIFC Market Rules (MAR), V13
title: MAR Schedule 4 para 4(a)(iii) points to 'technology and governance requirements set out in AMI 2-1.2'; those are in AMI 2-1.1
summary: MAR Schedule 4 para 4(a)(iii) requires a Security Token prospectus to explain 'how the operator of the facility meets the technology and governance requirements set out in AMI 2-1.2'. In AMI V11 the technology and governance requirements are AMI 2-1.1 ('Technology and governance requirements'); AMI 2-1.2 is 'Operating a facility for Investment Tokens that permits direct access'. The same mismatch existed when Schedule 4 was introduced (AMI V8, 1 Jan 2024).

act: AIFC Authorised Market Institution Rules (AMI), V11
title: AMI 2-1.2.2(4) refers to the annual audit 'required under AMI 2-1.5'; AMI has no 2-1.5 (audit is 2-1.4)
summary: AMI 2-1.2.2(4) requires systems and controls embedded in DLT to be "included within the scope of the annual audit and written report required under AMI 2-1.5". Chapter 2-1 (in AMI since V8, 1 January 2024) ends with 2-1.4 "Technology audit reports", which contains the annual audit and written report. In V8 to V11 there is no AMI 2-1.5.

act: AIFC Authorised Market Institution Rules (AMI), V11
title: 'Environmental Instrument Tokens' (AMI 2.6.1(3)) is undefined; the Glossary instead has a second 'Commodity Derivative Token' entry in the E-position
summary: AMI 2.6.1(3) requires a direct-access Member whose access is only for "Commodity Derivative Tokens or Environmental Instrument Tokens" to be a Professional Client. "Environmental Instrument Token" is not defined in the Glossary. Glossary V23 has two entries "Commodity Derivative Token" with the same text: one in alphabetical place under C, and a second one directly after "Environmental Instrument". The AFSA online Glossary has the same duplicate. The second entry may have been meant to define "Environmental Instrument Token"; the text does not show this.

act: AIFC Rules on Multilateral and Organised Trading Facilities (MOTF), V3
title: MOTF 8.1(2)-(3), 6.3 and 20.1: cross-references garbled ('8.1((a)a(a)', '8.1(a)(i)(i)(a)(i)(i)', '6.2(a)(i)', '20.1(1)(1)')
summary: MOTF 8.1(1) has paragraphs (a) to (c). 8.1(2) says "For the purposes of MOTF 8.1((a)a(a)"; 8.1(3)(a) "MOTF 8.1(a)a(b)"; 8.1(3)(b) "MOTF 8.1(a)(i)(i)(a)(i)(i)"; 8.1(3)(c) "MOTF 8.1(a)(i)(i)(1)". MOTF 6.2 has items (i) and (ii) without (a), yet 6.3 waives "MOTF 6.2(a)(i)". MOTF 20.1(1) has no sub-paragraph, yet 20.1(2) to (4) refer to "MOTF 20.1(1)(1)". The AFSA online text is the same. For 8.1(2) and 6.3 the target follows from the content (8.1(1)(a), error checking; 6.2(i), public consultation). For 8.1(3)(a) it is unclear whether "made public" qualifies 8.1(1)(b) (consolidation of data) or (c) (availability to the public).

act: AIFC Recognition Rules (REC)
title: REC 1.1.4(a): should the comparison also cover Chapter 2 of Part 3 of the Framework Regulations?
summary: REC 1.1.4 is made for section 89(3)(a) of the Framework Regulations, which asks whether investors get protection equivalent to the requirements for licensing an Authorised Market Institution "in Chapter 2 of Part 3". REC 1.1.4(a) asks the applicant to compare its home rules "with Part 4 of the Framework Regulations and Chapters 2 and 3 or 4 (as appropriate) of the AMI Rules". Part 4 is "Controlled and Designated Functions". The AMI chapters cover much of what section 89(3)(a) protects, and controlled functions are also relevant, but Chapter 2 of Part 3 is not named.

act: AIFC Market Rules (MAR), V13
title: AFSA online Market Rules do not contain MAR 1.9.3 and 1.9.4 (Amendments No. 7, 29 June 2022)
summary: The AFSA online Market Rules do not contain MAR 1.9.3 (Expert’s responsibility) and 1.9.4 (Exceptions from liability), which Amendments No. 7 inserted with effect from 29 June 2022. In the online text, 1.9.2 (Limitations on the application of MAR 1.9.1) is followed directly by 1.10 (AIFC ESG Debentures). The consolidated versions V8 to V13 on aifc.kz contain both rules. The online text applied another change made by the same instrument (MAR 2.1(2), which excludes Listed Funds and Exempt Offerors from MAR 2), but not its change to MAR 3.1-1(1), which in the act also excludes an Exempt Offeror from MAR 3. The online Schedule 4, paragraph 1(a)(ii) still refers to "consent under MAR 1.9.3", and the Glossary defines "Expert" by MAR 1.9.3; a reader of the online rulebook cannot find that rule. Our earlier observation on the Glossary entry "Expert" (AIFC-GLO-06) relied on the online text and is withdrawn: the definition resolves in the act. MAR 1.9.4(4)(a) has a separate wrong reference (see AIFC2-MKT-05).

act: AIFC Conduct of Business Rules (COB), V17
title: COB 1.2.2(c) applies COB 8 (Client Assets) to Authorised Crowdfunding Platforms, but the reading rule does not reach the scope of COB 8, which is defined by Investment Business
summary: COB 1.2.2(c) disapplies COB for an Authorised Crowdfunding Platform except COB 3, COB 4, COB 7, "COB 8 (Client Assets)" and COB Schedule 2, and the reading rule that follows provides that in these chapters "Regulated Activities" shall be read as "Market Activities". COB 8 does not use that term to set its scope: it applies to a firm that holds Money for a Client "in the course of, or in connection with, the carrying on of Investment Business or Provides Money Services" (COB 8.1.2(a), 8.1.4), and COB 8.2.1 defines Client Money by Investment Business. Operating a Loan or Investment Crowdfunding Platform is a Market Activity and is not in the Glossary definition of Investment Business. Read literally, the Client Money Rules do not attach to money a platform holds for lenders or investors, for example before the target funding amount is reached (AMI 7.3.22) or when it collects repayments for lenders (AMI 7.4.2), unless the platform also holds a licence for Investment Business or Money Services (AMI 7.2.1). AMI 2.9.1 requires satisfactory arrangements for safeguarding users' assets, and AMI 7.3.4(1)(n) requires disclosure of the "arrangements and safeguards for Client Assets held or controlled by an Authorised Crowdfunding Platform", but these rules do not set out the client money rules or the distribution rules in COB 8.2.16. Example: lenders transfer 900,000 USD to a platform for a loan with a target of 1,000,000 USD; the platform fails before the target is reached; whether the 900,000 USD is Client Money protected by COB 8.2.16 depends on whether COB 8 is read as reaching Market Activities.

act: AIFC Collective Investment Scheme Rules (CIS), V8
title: Disclosure item for a Fund Manager acting itself as custodian of Real Property points to CIS 7.3(e), which the same amending instrument deleted
summary: CIS 5.3(l)(viii) requires three disclosures "If the Fund Manager itself acts as the custodian of Real Property, in accordance with CIS 7.3.(e)". CIS 7.3(e) reads "[intentionally omitted]": Amendments No. 3 (in force 1 June 2023) inserted 5.3(l)(viii) with this reference and, on the same page, deleted the whole of 7.3(e), which was the custody exemption for a Self-managed Fund. The reference therefore has no target. A Fund may still have no Eligible Custodian under 8.2(b), or under a waiver (8.2(e) or 1.3), but CIS does not describe any of these cases as the Fund Manager itself acting as custodian, so it is unclear when the disclosure applies. The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0001 deletes the words "Subject to Rule (e), and" in 7.3(d) but moves the disclosure item, with the same reference to 7.3(e), into the new CIS 5.6.2(h).

act: AIFC Collective Investment Scheme Rules (CIS), V8
title: CIS 5.3(l) is headed 'Information relating to a Feeder Fund' but sets property-fund disclosures; 'Property Fund' is not defined
summary: Paragraph (l) of CIS 5.3 opens 'Information relating to a Feeder Fund:' and then lists only real-estate items: investment in Real Property, the 'Property Fund's' net assets in property-related assets, vacant or mortgaged properties, valuer under 6.10(b), insurance of Real Property, single-property funds, REIT vehicle. Nothing in (l) concerns Feeder Funds (whose disclosures sit in 2.4-1(c)(v)). The term 'Property Fund' used in (l)(ii), (iv), (v), (vi)(E), (vii) and Schedule 1 (j)(i) is not defined in CIS or in Glossary V23. Under s.24 of the AIFC Regulations on AIFC Acts the heading is part of the act, so the text names one scope (Feeder Funds) and the content implies another (funds investing in Real Property, incl. REITs).

act: AIFC Collective Investment Scheme Rules (CIS), V8
title: CIS 5.3(l)(ii) refers to 'property related assets, referred to in 3.1(b)' — CIS 3.1 has no paragraph (b)
summary: 5.3(l)(ii) requires disclosure of the percentage of net assets that may consist of 'property related assets, referred to in 3.1(b)'. CIS 3.1 is the one-paragraph 'Application' rule of chapter 3 (arrangements not amounting to a CIS) and has no (b); no other rulebook is named. 'Property related assets' is not defined in CIS or Glossary V23.

act: AIFC Collective Investment Scheme Rules (CIS), V8
title: CIS 5.1 disapplies 5.3(b)(i) (investment objective, strategy, leverage) for Non-Exempt Funds; in the draft, 5.1 refers to the deleted rule 5.3
summary: CIS 5.1(a) applies 5.3 to all Funds "excluding 5.3(b)(i) and (j)", and 5.1(b) applies "5.3(b)(i) and (j)" to Exempt Funds only. 5.3(b)(i) is the core disclosure of the investment objective, policy and strategy, asset types, risks and leverage, including the maximum level of leverage. The items that are Exempt-only by nature are 5.3(i) (the Exempt Fund legend) and 5.3(j) (the legend for an Exempt Fund of a Foreign Fund Manager). Read literally, a Non-Exempt (retail) Fund is relieved of 5.3(b)(i) while Exempt Funds must give it. The opening words of 5.3(b) and Schedule 1(j) still bind every Fund, so what is literally lost is the specific list, including the maximum level of leverage. The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0001 deletes rule 5.3 and moves its content to the new 5.4, 5.5 and Schedule 1-1, while 5.1(a) and (b) still refer to "5.3 (excluding 5.3(b)(i) and (j))" and "5.3(b)(i) and (j)". If the draft is adopted as published, both references will point to a deleted rule.

act: AIFC Collective Investment Scheme Rules (CIS), V8
title: Custody for domestic Exempt Funds: CIS 7.3(d) requires an Eligible Custodian "in accordance with Rule 8.2", but chapter 8 applies only to other Funds; do its exceptions apply?
summary: CIS chapter 7 applies to Domestic Fund Managers "in respect of all Funds" (7.1), so 7.3(d) — delegate custody to an Eligible Custodian "in accordance with Rule 8.2" — reaches domestic Exempt Funds. Chapter 8, including the exceptions in 8.2(b) and (e), applies only to Non-Exempt Funds and REITs of Domestic Fund Managers and to Exempt Funds of Foreign Fund Managers (8.1). The words "in accordance with Rule 8.2" can be read to bring the exceptions in 8.2(b) and (e) with them, and the general waiver in CIS 1.3 is also available, but the text does not say so. Separately, PRU(INV) Table 3.3 assumes that a Single Family Office Fund does not need an Eligible Custodian; CIS has no such rule. This overlaps with our earlier item on PRU(INV) Table 3.3 (AIFC-PRU-01).

act: AIFC Collective Investment Scheme Rules (CIS), V8
title: CIS 7.7: 'Related Person Transaction' covers 'any other Fund managed by the Fund', not by the Fund Manager as the heading says
summary: CIS 7.7(a) and (d) refer to "any other Fund managed by the Fund or any of its Associates". A Fund does not manage other Funds; the heading of 7.7 speaks of Funds "managed by the Fund Manager". The meaning survives through the heading and the Associate limb, but the wording has no referent.

act: AIFC Collective Investment Scheme Rules (CIS), V8
title: Reports on Single Family Office and Corporate Treasury Centre Funds: the draft extends CIS 10.4 and 10.5 to every Domestic Fund, but 10.5(b) and the Guidance to 2.4.17 do not match
summary: Under the current CIS, reports on Single Family Office and Corporate Treasury Centre Funds (10.5-1(j), 10.5-1.1) have no deadline, frequency or recipient: both Funds must be Exempt Funds, and 10.5, which sets the timing and recipients of Fund reports, applies to Non-Exempt Funds only (10.1(ii)). CIS also does not require these Funds to be audited (10.4 and 10.1(i)). The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0001 extends the audit rule in 10.4 and the periodic reports in 10.5(a) to each Domestic Fund, which answers most of this point. Two questions remain on the draft. First, 10.5(b) still sets the four-month deadline for the annual report "for the Non-Exempt Fund", while 10.5(c) no longer says "Non-Exempt", so the deadline for the annual report of other Domestic Funds is unclear. Second, the Guidance to the new 2.4.17 says that for a Corporate Treasury Centre Fund "the standard Fund Manager reporting requirements under CIS 10.5 also do not apply", while the draft 10.5(a) covers each Domestic Fund and states no exception.

act: AIFC Collective Investment Scheme Rules (CIS), V8
title: "Single Family Office Fund" and "Corporate Treasury Centre Fund" are not defined, and the CTC Fund is spelled three ways
summary: CIS gives relief to Single Family Office Funds and Corporate Treasury Centre Funds (7.2-1.2, 7.2-1.3, 4.2(d)(i), 6.2(a)), but the two terms are not defined in CIS or the Glossary. A third spelling, "Corporate Treasury Fund", appears in 5.3(b) and the heading of 10.5-1.1. The classes can largely be identified from the defined terms "Single Family Office" and "Corporate Treasury Centre" and from 7.2-1.2, 7.2-1.3, 6.14 and 10.5-1(j), so the gap is one of definition and spelling.

act: AIFC Collective Investment Scheme Rules (CIS), V8
title: AFSA online CIS Schedule 2(a)(i) still reads "Non-Compliant Country"; Amendments No. 7 deleted "Non-" from 1 January 2025
summary: CIS Schedule 2(a)(i) lists, as a criterion for a Recognised Jurisdiction, that "the jurisdiction is listed as a Compliant Country or Territory by the Financial Action Task Force" (V8). Amendments No. 7 (approved 15 December 2024, in force 1 January 2025) deleted the word "Non-" from this item; the amending instrument shows it as struck through. The AFSA online CIS still reads "Non-Compliant Country or Territory" and shows no deleted (struck-through) text at that place. Versions V3 to V7 of the act carried the word "Non-" from 2019 to the end of 2024; Amendments No. 7 fixed the act, but not the online text.

act: AIFC Collective Investment Scheme Rules (CIS), V8
title: AFSA online CIS shows rule 10.1 in the 2018 wording, without Exempt Funds of Foreign Fund Managers added by Amendments No. 2 (2019)
summary: The AFSA online CIS still shows 10.1 in the 2018 wording: "This chapter applies to all Funds managed by Fund Managers located in the AIFC." Since Amendments No. 2 (2019), 10.1 also covers (b) Exempt Funds of Foreign Fund Managers. The online text therefore leaves those Funds outside 10.2, 10.3 and 10.6.

act: AIFC Collective Investment Scheme Rules (CIS), V8
title: AFSA online CIS misses other Amendments No. 7 changes: Venture Capital Fund (2.4(b)(iii)), 7.6(b) "Associates", and rule 1.6 without text
summary: The AFSA online CIS includes many changes made by Amendments No. 7 (in force 1 January 2025), but not these: (1) 2.4(b)(iii) still describes a Venture Capital Fund as "an Exempt Fund and a Domestic Fund" that invests "in the equity share capital" of unlisted businesses; Amendments No. 7 deleted "and a Domestic Fund" and replaced "equity share capital" with "Securities and Units", while the online text already shows the feeder route added by the same amendment; (2) 7.6(b) still says "Associates" where Amendments No. 7 put "Related Parties"; (3) rule 1.6 (when a Fund invests in Digital Assets indirectly), inserted by Amendments No. 7, has a heading but no text under it.

act: AIFC Islamic Finance Rules (IFR)
title: IFR 7.5(3) and the draft Shari'ah Governance Rules: does a Fund that relies on Shari'ah screening keep its relief from appointing an SSB?
summary: Under the current IFR, 7.5(3) releases the Fund Manager of a Non-Exempt Fund from appointing an SSB where it relies on a widely accepted Shari'ah screening process, while 7.3(1), 7.6(2) and 7.7(1) refer to "the Fund's SSB" without an exception. The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0003 deletes IFR 7.5 to 7.7 and places Shari'ah governance in new Shari'ah Governance Rules, which apply to "a Fund Manager of a Domestic Fund which is operated or held out as being operated as an Islamic Fund" (rule 1(1)(b)). After adoption the conflict inside IFR falls away with 7.5 to 7.7. Two questions remain: the new Rules contain no counterpart of the screening relief in 7.5(3), so it is unclear whether such Funds must now appoint an SSB; and IFR 7.3(1), which the draft does not amend, still requires approval by "the Fund's SSB".

act: AIFC Glossary (GLO), V23
title: IFR 7.3 requires SSB approval of a Fund's "Prospectus", a Glossary term for securities prospectuses; Funds issue "Offering Materials"
summary: IFR 7.3(1) and (2) require a Fund’s Constitution "and Prospectus" to be approved by an SSB and reviewed every year; the Guidance under 7.2 also speaks of the Fund’s "most recent Prospectus". In the Glossary, "Prospectus" is the document referred to in MAR 1.3, which an unlisted Fund does not issue; such a Fund gives investors "Offering Materials" (CIS 5.3), and IFR itself uses that term in 7.8. Read with 7.8, "Prospectus" in 7.3 can be understood as the Fund’s Offering Materials, but the defined term points elsewhere. CIS has moved to the same term for Funds: Amendments No. 7 to CIS (in force 1 January 2025) replaced "Prospectus" with "Offering Materials" in the Feeder Fund rules. IFR 7.3 was not aligned.

act: AIFC Banking Business Prudential Rules (BBR), V6
title: Non-significant investments: holdings below 10% of CET1 are deducted in full, holdings at or above 10% only above the threshold
summary: BBR 4.29(4) applies when, after other regulatory adjustments, the total of the deductions under that rule is less than 10% of the Bank's CET1 capital; the Bank must then deduct the investments in full (4.29(4)(b)-(c)). BBR 4.29(5) applies when the total is 10% or more and deducts only the amount by which it exceeds 10% (the excess). With CET1 of 100, holdings of 9.9 are deducted in full (9.9), holdings of 10 lead to no deduction and holdings of 11 to a deduction of 1. A bank can therefore keep more CET1 by holding more. IBB 4.43 and 4.44 have the same structure. Carried through to the capital ratios: for a bank with CET1 of USD 50 million, other credit risk-weighted assets of USD 450 million, a market risk requirement of USD 4 million and an operational risk requirement of USD 7.5 million, holdings of USD 4.9 million are deducted in full and the bank falls below its capital requirement under 4.9 and the 8% Total Capital ratio (USD 45.1 million against 47.5 million); holdings of USD 5.0 million are not deducted and the bank meets them (USD 50 million against 48.7 million). Line 37 of Form 30 in the Manual for Preparation of Returns deducts only the amount above the 10% threshold.

act: AIFC Banking Business Prudential Rules (BBR), V6
title: Basic indicator approach: GI is defined as an average, and the formula divides it by n again
summary: BBR 7.6(2) sets the operational risk capital requirement as GI x alpha / n. GI is defined as "the Bank's average annual gross income" for the years (out of the previous 3) in which it is positive, and n is the number of those years. The average is therefore divided by n a second time, and the result falls as the number of positive years grows: with gross income of USD 50 million in each of three years the requirement is 50 x 15% / 3 = USD 2.5 million; with USD 50 million in one year and losses in the other two it is USD 7.5 million. Sub-rule (3) speaks of excluding loss years "from both the numerator and denominator when calculating the average". The difference concerns the operational risk component, which enters risk-weighted assets at 12.5 times the requirement (BBR 4.7(2)(b)), not the whole capital requirement. IBB 9.10(2) has the same formula and definition. Carried through to the capital ratios: for a bank with gross income of USD 50 million in each of three years, other credit risk-weighted assets of USD 450 million, a market risk requirement of USD 4 million and Total Capital of USD 45 million, the requirement under 4.9 is USD 42.5 million as printed and USD 47.5 million if gross income is averaged once, so the bank meets or breaches the 8% Total Capital ratio depending on the reading (8.47% against 7.58%). The AFSA return (Annex 1.13 of the Manual for Preparation of Returns) computes a single "Average GI" over the positive years and does not divide it by n again.

act: AIFC Banking Business Prudential Rules (BBR), V6
title: LCR powers: appeal and procedure refer to '(4)(a)-(e)' and '(1)(d)' instead of 9.16(5)
summary: BBR 9.16(5)(a)-(e) lists the AFSA's powers on the liquidity coverage ratio. Sub-rules (6), (7) and (8) refer to "(4)(a), (b), (c) or (e)" and "(1)(d)", but 9.16(4) and 9.16(1) have no such paragraphs. The sister rule IBB 10.25(6)-(8) cites (5). The Framework Regulations still give procedure and appeal rights, so the meaning survives.

act: AIFC Banking Business Prudential Rules (BBR), V6
title: BBR cites BPG Chapter 9 Sections D, E and F for the LCR, NSFR and maturity mismatch; in the BPG these are Sections G, H and I
summary: BBR 9.16(5)(b) (the AFSA's power to adjust "requirements under section D of Chapter 9 of the BPG" for HQLA and net cash outflows), 9.19(2) (NSFR methodology, "Section E", twice) and 9.21(1)(a) (maturity-ladder methodology, "section F") cite BPG Chapter 9 by section letter; the notes to 9.16(3) and 9.21 do the same. In the published BPG (AFSA-L-GB-2019-0001, 28 January 2019) Sections D, E and F of Chapter 9 are Funding Strategy, Stress Testing and Contingency Funding Plan; the LCR, NSFR and Maturity Mismatch Approach are Sections G, H and I. The right sections can be found by their titles.

act: AIFC Banking Business Prudential Rules (BBR), V6
title: Securitisation exposures: Table 5C row 10 or Table 5H? No rule says which applies to an originator's or sponsor's retained positions
summary: BBR has two risk-weight tables for securitisation exposures. Table 5B item 9 sends "claims on securitisation exposures" to Table 5C row 10 (50% to 250%; unrated 150%). Rule 5.21(16) applies Table 5H (20% to 350%; B+ and below or unrated 1,250% or deduction) to on-balance-sheet retained securitisation exposures, which 5.21(12)-(13) link to a Bank that is an originator or sponsor, including its investments in the securitisation. Read as a specific rule, 5.21(16) governs those positions and Table 5C row 10 the positions of other investors. But no rule says so, and 5.21(7) speaks of applying Table 5H to "a securitisation exposure" in general. The weights differ widely, for example 50% against 20% for AAA and 150% against 1,250% for an unrated exposure.

act: AIFC Banking Business Prudential Rules (BBR), V6
title: Allocation of the 10% excess across tiers uses the bank's OWN capital as numerator and holdings as denominator; shares do not sum to 1
summary: BBR 4.29(5)(c) allocates the excess over 10% to each tier of capital by the formula Excess x A/B, where A is "the amount of CET 1 capital, additional tier 1 capital or tier 2 capital of the Bank" and B is "the total capital holdings of the Bank". Read literally, A is the bank's own capital in a tier, while B is its holdings in other entities, so the three shares do not add up to 1. For example, with own CET1, AT1 and T2 of 100, 10 and 20, holdings of 12 (CET1) and 3 (T2) and an excess of 5, the literal formula deducts 43.3 in total instead of 5. Under 4.29(1)(b) deductions are made from the tier for which the held capital would qualify, which points to A being the bank's holdings in that tier. "Capital holdings" is not defined. IBB 4.44(3) has the same wording. With holdings of USD 15 million, all in CET1 instruments, and own CET1 of USD 100 million, the literal formula deducts USD 33.3 million instead of 5 million; with holdings of USD 150 million it deducts USD 93.3 million instead of 140 million. For a bank with other credit risk-weighted assets of USD 900 million, a market risk requirement of USD 10 million and an operational risk requirement of USD 15 million (capital requirement USD 99.4 million), Total Capital after the allocation is USD 86.7 million under the literal formula and USD 125 million if A is the holdings of each tier.

act: AIFC Banking Business Prudential Rules (BBR), V6
title: Threshold deduction: 10% per item 'or' 15% aggregate; (4) deducts the excess over '(3)(a) or (b)' - outcome indeterminate
summary: 4.30(3) grants full recognition (300%/400% risk weight, no deduction) 'provided that (a) each item is no more than 10% ...; or (b) in total, the 3 items are no more than 15%'. With 'or', a bank whose items are each under 10% but total over 15% satisfies (a) and needs no deduction, while 4.30(4) requires deduction of 'any amount in excess of the threshold in (3)(a) or (b)', which can be read as the excess over 15%. The same 'or' is in IBB 4.46(3). (Also '(net of all regulatory adjustments except those under this Subdivision)': there are no Subdivisions in BBR.) With three items of USD 9 million each and CET1 of USD 100 million, the text yields a deduction of 0 (sub-rule (3)(a)) and of USD 12 million (sub-rule (4) by reference to (3)(b)). A bank with other credit risk-weighted assets of USD 800 million and a market risk requirement of USD 10 million then both meets and breaches its capital requirement under 4.9 (USD 100 million against 97.64 million; USD 88 million against 93.8 million). Lines 38-40 and 44 of Form 30 in the Manual for Preparation of Returns apply the 10% and 15% limits together.

act: AIFC Banking Business Prudential Rules (BBR), V6
title: Table 4A capital conservation ratios: rows share boundary values ('to' / '≥') and 7.0% sits between '≥6.375% to 7.0%' and '>7%'
summary: BBR Table 4A uses the bands "4.5% to 5.125%", "≥5.125% to 5.75%", "≥5.75% to 6.375%", "≥6.375% to 7.0%" and ">7%". If "to" includes the upper value, 5.125%, 5.75% and 6.375% fall in two rows; if it excludes it, as the "≥" signs suggest, exactly 7.0% falls in no row (rule 4.32(1) then limits the restriction to a buffer below the minimum). At exactly 5.125% the table (row 2, 80% conservation) and the BPG Chapter 4 guidance, paragraph 11(a) ("less than or equal to 5.125%", 100%), give different results. IBB Table 5.1 uses "X% or more but less than Y%" and "≥7%".

act: AIFC Banking Business Prudential Rules (BBR), V6
title: AT1 and T2 definitions cite Rule 4.28 (CET1 adjustments); the CET1 definition cites only Rule 4.29
summary: BBR 4.16(d) and 4.18(d) say AT1 and T2 capital are adjusted "in accordance with Rule 4.28", but 4.28 is "Adjustments to CET1 Capital". BBR 4.14(f) refers to Rule 4.29 for CET1; 4.29 does contain CET1 deductions, but the CET1 adjustments in 4.28 and 4.30 are not mentioned. The rules operate directly, so there is no practical effect.

act: AIFC Banking Business Prudential Rules (BBR), V6
title: Operational risk policy rule copied from market risk: Governing Body must ensure a bank-wide view of 'Market Risk exposures'
summary: BBR 7.1(5) repeats 6.1(4) word for word except for the name of the policy: the operational risk management policy must give "a comprehensive bank-wide view of its Market Risk exposures" and take into account "the risk of a significant deterioration in market liquidity of its exposures". BBR 7.1(4)(d) likewise ties the review of the operational risk policy to the "nature, scale and complexity of its Trading Book activities" (copied from 6.1(3)(d)). The substance is partly covered elsewhere: 7.5(1)(a) requires the bank to identify operational risks in all its products, activities, processes and systems, and 7.5(1)(f) requires reporting to the Governing Body.

act: AIFC Banking Business Prudential Rules (BBR), V6
title: Fallback signatories of prudential returns: 'Risk Manager' is called a Controlled Function, but in GEN it is a Designated Function
summary: BBR 3.7(2) requires, if the primary signatories are unavailable, signature by 'both of the individuals approved to exercise the following Controlled Functions: (a) the Risk Manager function; (b) the Compliance Officer function'. GEN 2.2.1 lists Controlled Functions as GEN 2.2.2-2.2.5 (SEO, Director, Finance Officer, Compliance Officer); Risk Manager is GEN 2.3.5 and may be held by a Designated Individual who is not AFSA-approved (GEN 2.1.2(2)). In GEN at the BBR's adoption (2018) there was no Risk Manager function at all.

act: AIFC Banking Business Prudential Rules (BBR), V6
title: BPG not updated: it says Credit Providers are not Banking Business firms and excludes them from the leverage ratio, which BBR 4.36 has applied to Providing Credit since December 2022
summary: BPG paragraph 6 says: "Credit Providers as defined in BBR 1.7 are not included in Banking Business firms according to BBR 1.4." BBR 1.4(3) has said since 2018 that a Banking Business firm may be a Credit Provider, and BPG paragraphs 2, 4 and 5 themselves include Credit Providers. The BPG tables also exclude Credit Providers from Section 4F (Rules 4.36-4.37, leverage ratio). That matched BBR 4.36 until the version with amendments as of 9 December 2022, which applies Section 4F to firms licensed for "Accepting Deposits" or "Providing Credit". The BPG (28 January 2019) has not been updated. The BBR prevail, so the problem is misleading guidance.

act: AIFC Islamic Banking Business Prudential Rules
title: IBB NSFR rule cites 'Section E of Appendix 1' (does not exist) and then 'Section B' in the same paragraph
summary: IBB 10.28(2) first says that the NSFR methodology is "set out in Section E of Appendix 1 of the IBB Module", and then refers to "Section B of Appendix 1" for the ASF and RSF factors. Appendix 1 has only Sections A (LCR), B (NSFR) and C (Maturity Mismatch). The meaning survives through the second sentence.

act: AIFC Insurance and Reinsurance Prudential Rules
title: Counterparty grade table omits Fitch 'BBB' (Grade 4 lists only BBB+ and BBB-) in PINS and TRR
summary: In Table A of PINS Schedule 5 (counterparty grades), Grade 4 lists Fitch "BBB+" and "BBB-" but not "BBB"; the S&P column lists all three. TRR Schedule 5 Table A is identical. The order of the table points to Grade 4.

act: AIFC Insurance and Reinsurance Prudential Rules
title: Two 'Category 3' in long-term categories; general categories 1-2 exclude a non-existent 'Category 4 (Permanent Health)' (PINS and TRR)
summary: PINS Schedule 2 numbers both "Linked long-term" and "Permanent health" as Long-Term Insurance Category 3; there is no Category 4. General Insurance Categories 1 (Accident) and 2 (Sickness) in Schedule 1 exclude "contracts falling within Long-Term Insurance Category 4 (Permanent Health)". The name in brackets identifies the intended category, so the meaning survives. TRR Schedules 1 and 2 repeat this (Family Takaful Category 3 twice; General Takaful Categories 1 and 2 exclude Family Takaful Category 4).

act: AIFC Insurance and Reinsurance Prudential Rules
title: Relief from the asset risk charge for assets excluded from Eligible Capital "in accordance with the table B1": the phrase can be read two ways (PINS and TRR)
summary: PINS Schedule 5, paragraph 4.4: an insurer "need not include an amount in the asset risk charge for any asset excluded from Eligible Capital in accordance with the table B1 in paragraph 4.1". Table B1 sets charges and excludes nothing from Eligible Capital; the exclusions are in Schedule 3, paragraph 5. If the words "in accordance with the table B1" go with "the asset risk charge", the relief covers assets excluded under Schedule 3, which is the evident purpose. If they go with "excluded", the relief covers no asset. TRR Schedule 5, paragraph 4.4 is the same.

act: AIFC Insurance and Reinsurance Prudential Rules
title: General insurers must seek MER advice from "its Approved Actuary"; it is unclear whether insurers not otherwise required to have one must appoint one (PINS and TRR)
summary: PINS Schedule 5, paragraph 10 applies to General Insurance Business. Paragraph 10.2(2) requires an insurer to "seek advice from its Approved Actuary" about its maximum event retention if it issues policies without a maximum amount insured, insures risks in multiple lines of business or has a complex portfolio. Under PINS 2.2.2(2) an Approved Actuary is mandatory for a general insurer only in certain cases, and PINS 9.2 deals with insurers "not required to have an Approved Actuary". The text does not say whether paragraph 10.2(2) itself requires such an insurer to appoint one, or whether it may use the independent actuary described in PINS 9.2.3. TRR Schedule 5, paragraph 10.2(2) is the same.

act: AIFC Insurance and Reinsurance Prudential Rules
title: Captive PCR: PINS 14.4.3(1) exempts Class 1, 2 and 3 captives, while the AFSA Guidance (2020) says only Class 1 is exempt
summary: PINS 14.4.3(1) says Class 1, 2 and 3 Captive Insurers "are not required to calculate" the Prescribed Capital Requirement; 14.4.3(2) says each Cell of a Protected Cell Company "must calculate" it. Read with the heading, (2) is the specific rule for PCC cells. The AFSA's Guidance to the AIFC Captive Insurance Regime (13 December 2020) says only pure captives (Class 1) are exempt, which differs from 14.4.3(1).

act: AIFC Glossary (GLO), V23
title: Glossary still defines 'Captive Insurer' as group-only, contrary to PINS 14.1.1 (Class 2 and 3 since 2020); FEES fee rows depend on it
summary: Glossary V23: Captive Insurer = Licence to carry on Insurance Business 'only for the business or operations of the Group to which it belongs'. PINS 14.1.1-14.1.2 (since 13.12.2020): Class 2 may take up to 20% of GWP from third-party risks; Class 3 insures persons in similar businesses (group captives). The PINS 'Working Schedule 1' list of defined terms also keeps the group-only text. FEES V18 charges 'Captive Insurance Business' USD 7,000 (application) / 4,200 (annual) versus 'Insurance Business' 14,000 / 9,800.

act: AIFC Insurance and Reinsurance Prudential Rules
title: Notice to policyholders must include 'the Scheme Summary referred to in rule 11.8' - there is no rule 11.8 (PINS and TRR)
summary: PINS 11.4.1(1)(b) and TRR 11.4.1(1)(b) refer to 'rule 11.8'; chapter 11 ends at 11.4.2. The Scheme Summary is defined in 11.2.3(a)(ii) and regulated in 11.3.3.

act: AIFC Takaful and Retakaful Prudential Rules
title: TRR: Takaful Fund ring-fence exceptions refer to a non-existent "Rule 2.1.2 (1)", 2.2.3 to "rule 2.1.1", and 1.1.3(2) to 1.1.6(1) for the definition of Takaful Business
summary: The prohibition on using Takaful Fund assets for other purposes is TRR 2.2.2(1), which itself announces "the exceptions provided for in the rest of this rule below"; the funds are established under 2.2.1. Yet 2.2.2(2), (3) and (4) say "Rule 2.1.2 (1) above does not ...", and 2.2.3 speaks of a Takaful Fund "established and maintained under rule 2.1.1". TRR 2.1 ("Overall Governance") has no numbered sub-rules. Separately, 1.1.3(2) refers to Takaful Business "as defined in Rules 1.1.6 (1)", but 1.1.6 lists principles and 1.1.5(1) defines a Takaful Operator; the activity of Takaful Business is defined in GEN Schedule 1, paragraph 25. The meaning survives in each case.

act: AIFC Prudential Rules for Insurance Intermediaries
title: PRU(INT) auditor certification covers quarterly returns submitted 'by the PRU Investment Firm' (copied from PRU INV)
summary: PRU(INT) 5.2(2): the auditor's certification must relate to the annual returns and "each set of unaudited quarterly returns that have been submitted to the AFSA by the PRU Investment Firm in the previous year". A PRU Investment Firm is a category under the Prudential Rules for Investment Firms; PRU(INT) applies to Insurance Intermediaries and Insurance Managers, called together "Authorised Firm" (1.3(1)). 5.2(1) and the first sentence of 5.2(2) speak of an Authorised Firm, so the meaning survives. This is the converse of our observation AIFC-PRU-03, where PRU (Investment Firms) 3.2 refers to "the Insurance Intermediary".

act: AIFC Prudential Rules for Insurance Intermediaries
title: PRU(INT) 4.2(1): duty to vet the PI insurer is placed on 'the Insurance Intermediary' only, though the rule starts with 'an Authorised Firm'
summary: PRU(INT) 4.2(1) reads: "Before an Authorised Firm takes out or renews a professional indemnity insurance policy with an insurer, the Insurance Intermediary must be satisfied ... that the insurer is a suitable Person to provide the insurance policy to the Insurance Intermediary". Under 1.3(1) "Authorised Firm" is used where rules apply to both Insurance Intermediaries and Insurance Managers. Read with the opening words, 4.2(2)-(3) and 1.3(1), the duty probably covers Insurance Managers too, but the text names only the Insurance Intermediary. In the release of 10 December 2017 the whole sentence referred to the Insurance Intermediary; the amendments as of 2 December 2018 changed only the opening words.

act: AIFC Prudential Rules for Insurance Intermediaries
title: "Insurance Manager" (an addressee of PRU(INT)) has no definition; PRU(INT) 1.3(2) uses "Insurance Mediation" instead of the GEN activity "Insurance Intermediation"
summary: PRU(INT) 1.3(1) applies the rules to "Insurance Intermediaries and Insurance Managers". The Glossary defines Insurance Intermediary but has no entry for Insurance Manager, and GEN defines the activity "Insurance Management" (Schedule 1, paragraph 24) but not the term "Insurance Manager". The addressee can be identified as a firm licensed for Insurance Management, but no text says so; the AFSA's Guidance to the AIFC Captive Insurance Regime states that "Insurance Manager is defined in the AIFC General Rules". Separately, 1.3(2) speaks of "an Authorisation to carry on Insurance Mediation"; the Regulated Activity is "Insurance Intermediation" (GEN Schedule 1, paragraph 15).

act: AIFC Banking Business Prudential Rules (BBR), V6
title: Capital conservation ratios: Table 4A is entered by the CET1 capital ratio, while the buffer under 4.31(2) excludes CET1 used for the T1 and Total Capital ratios
summary: BBR 4.31(2) provides that the capital conservation buffer must be made up of CET1 capital above the amounts used to meet the CET1, T1 and Total Capital ratios, and 4.32(1) requires a bank whose buffer falls below the required minimum to restrict its distributions. Under 4.32(2) and Table 4A, however, the minimum capital conservation ratio is selected by the bank's CET1 capital ratio, which does not exclude the CET1 used to meet the T1 and Total Capital ratios; a ratio above 7% gives 0%. For a bank whose capital is all CET1, the buffer becomes positive only above 8% of risk-weighted assets and reaches 2.5% at 10.5%. With risk-weighted assets of USD 1,000 million, CET1 of USD 85 million (8.5%) and no AT1 or T2 capital, the bank's ratios are above the minima, its buffer under 4.31(2) is USD 5 million against USD 25 million, so it is in breach of 4.31(1) and 4.32(1) requires it to restrict distributions; yet Table 4A sets no positive minimum retention (0%). BPG Chapter 4 paragraph 11(c) states that a bank with a CET1 capital ratio of more than 7% can distribute 100% of its earnings; 4.33(1) also compares CET1 with the CET1 ratio plus the buffer. IBB 5.2 to 5.4 and Table 5.1 have the same structure. Basel III paragraph 131 measures the CET1 ratio of the table excluding the CET1 needed for the 6% Tier 1 and 8% Total Capital requirements.
